title: Remember, Reason, Run: Inside One Living Workspace (July 2026)
summary: Your Taskade workspace remembers what you make, reasons through every step, and runs while you sleep. Inside Workspace DNA: memory, intelligence, execution.
body_markdown:
Your workspace used to wait. You opened it, typed something, closed it, and nothing moved until you came back. That is no longer how it works. A Taskade workspace now **remembers** what you make, **reasons** through every step with agents, and **runs** while you sleep, which is the whole distance between a task list and a system.[Build yours with AI](https://www.taskade.com/create?entry_kind=content&source=blog&entry=%2Fblog%2Fremember-reason-run) or[clone a living one](https://www.taskade.com/apps) in a click.


> **TL;DR:** A living workspace is[Workspace DNA](https://www.taskade.com/blog/workspace-dna-architecture) running as one loop: connected projects hold the **memory** ,[AI agents](https://www.taskade.com/agents) supply the **intelligence** , and[automations](https://www.taskade.com/automate) across 100+ integrations handle the **execution** .[TSK-1](https://www.taskade.com/blog/introducing-tsk-1) coordinates all three, so one prompt becomes an app that keeps working after you close the laptop.[Clone a live one free](https://www.taskade.com/apps) .


## What Is a Living Workspace?


A living workspace is a workspace that keeps working when you are not in it. Instead of holding your notes and waiting for you, it stores your data as connected projects, reasons over that data with[AI agents](https://www.taskade.com/agents) , and runs automations against it on a schedule. In[Taskade Genesis](https://www.taskade.com/ai/apps) that architecture has a name, and it is the same three layers in every app on this page.


Layer What it is What it does for you


**▲ Memory** Connected projects, files, and agent history Everything you make becomes context your agents can read


**■ Intelligence** AI agents running on[TSK-1](https://www.taskade.com/blog/introducing-tsk-1) Reads that context and decides the next step


**● Execution** Automations across[100+ integrations](https://www.taskade.com/integrations) Carries the step out, then writes the result back


That is **Workspace DNA** , and the important word is *loop* . Memory feeds intelligence, intelligence triggers execution, and execution creates new memory. Each pass leaves the workspace knowing slightly more than it did before, which is why the app you built in March is more useful in July without you touching it.


Most tools stop at the first arrow. They generate something and hand it to you frozen, which is the whole argument behind[the living software era](https://www.taskade.com/blog/living-software-era) and[how SaaS quietly evolved into living software](https://www.taskade.com/blog/saas-evolved-living-software) . The shift is easiest to see side by side.


```text
Yesterday                              Today
─────────                              ─────
A list you update by hand    ─▶        Projects that remember
A chat you re-explain daily  ─▶        Agents that already know
A reminder you set yourself  ─▶        Automations that fire on their own
A file you export to a tool  ─▶        An app that is already live


```


## Memory. Your Projects Remember.


Memory is not a feature you switch on in Taskade. Every project, document, file, and agent conversation you create becomes context the rest of the workspace can read. A job references the customer it belongs to. An invoice references the deal that closed. Nothing has to be re-pasted into a prompt, because the prompt and the database are the same place.


The **Neon CRM Dashboard** above is a live app you can[clone in one click](https://www.taskade.com/app/neon-crm-dashboard-nsrm12wns3e1cgni) . Its pipeline is not a spreadsheet with a nicer skin, it is the memory layer with a view attached. The same records render in multiple views (List, Board, Table, and Mind Map in the toolbar, plus Docs, Gantt Chart, Calendar, Actionsheet, and Org Chart under More Views), so the thing your agent reads and the thing you look at are never out of sync.


In the memory layer What it means in practice


**Connected projects** A job knows its customer, an invoice knows its deal


**Files and documents** A dropped file becomes searchable context, not a dead attachment


**Agent history** What you told an agent last week is still there this week


This is why[projects behave like databases](https://www.taskade.com/blog/projects-as-databases) rather than lists, and it is the practical version of what people mean by[types of memory in AI agents](https://www.taskade.com/blog/ai-agent-memory) . For the deeper reference, see[agent memory](https://www.taskade.com/wiki/ai-agents/agent-memory) and the[memory, workflows, and payments](https://www.taskade.com/blog/memory-workflows-payments) drop that first wired it together.


## Intelligence. Your Agents Reason.


Intelligence is the layer that reads your memory and decides what to do with it. A Taskade AI agent ships with a **built-in toolkit** , so it can search the web, read a file, run a custom slash command, and update a project without you wiring any of it. Underneath every one of those agents sits **TSK-1** , the Taskade System Kernel.


TSK-1 is not another AI model. It is the kernel *above* the models, and it routes each task across **frontier models from top AI labs** without asking you to pick one. Auto is the default. Fast edits get an instant answer, a hard question gets deeper reasoning, and a long build gets the most capable path, so the setting quietly disappears and you stay on the outcome. The full explainer is in[Introducing Taskade TSK-1](https://www.taskade.com/blog/introducing-tsk-1) , with the reference pages at[AI models in Taskade Genesis](https://www.taskade.com/learn/genesis/ai-models) and[TSK-1](https://www.taskade.com/wiki/genesis/tsk-1) .


What makes an agent useful is not the model, it is that the agent already stands inside your data. Point one at your pipeline and it answers from the deals you actually have, which is what separates[AI app builders with memory](https://www.taskade.com/blog/best-ai-app-builders) from generators that forget you between prompts. Browse ready-made ones in[task automation agents](https://www.taskade.com/agents/task-automation) , or read[the anatomy of a Taskade Genesis app](https://www.taskade.com/blog/anatomy-of-genesis-app) .


## Execution. Your Workflows Run.


Execution is what happens after you close the laptop. An automation waits for a trigger, a new lead, a dropped file, or a scheduled time, an agent reads the connected projects, and an action pushes the result back out across **100+ bidirectional integrations** . Triggers pull events in, actions push data out, and the updated record lands in the same project your team is already looking at.


The trigger What runs on its own


**A schedule fires** The nightly report is built and waiting before you wake up


**A file lands in a project** It is sorted, logged, and routed to the right person


**A deal is marked won** The invoice goes out and the record updates itself


You describe the rule in plain language and it runs. The step-by-step lives in[automation triggers](https://www.taskade.com/learn/automation/triggers) ,[automation actions](https://www.taskade.com/learn/automation/actions) , and the[Schedule trigger](https://www.taskade.com/learn/automation/schedule) , which fires as often as every few minutes or on the exact days you choose. For a longer walkthrough of handing the repetitive work over, read[set it once, it runs while you work](https://www.taskade.com/blog/set-it-once) , and browse ready-made flows in[agentic workflows](https://www.taskade.com/automate/agentic-workflows) .


## Connect Claude and ChatGPT to Your Workspace


The **Taskade MCP Server** lets the AI tools you already use reach into your workspace. Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, VS Code, and other MCP-compatible clients connect **in** to Taskade, read your live projects, and act on them from wherever you happen to be working. The hosted Taskade MCP Server is available on every paid plan.


The direction matters, so it is worth stating plainly: the client comes to your workspace. That is what turns Taskade from one more tab into the memory the rest of your AI tools share. Background is in[Taskade speaks MCP](https://www.taskade.com/blog/taskade-mcp-server) and the[MCP server reference](https://www.taskade.com/wiki/genesis/mcp-server) .

## Frequently Asked Questions


What is a living workspace in Taskade?


A living workspace is one that keeps working when you are not in it. One prompt becomes an app that is already live, with no export step and no separate hosting to manage.


What is Workspace DNA?


Workspace DNA is the three-layer architecture behind every[Taskade Genesis](https://www.taskade.com/ai/apps) app: Memory, Intelligence, and Execution. Connected projects hold the memory, AI agents supply the intelligence, and automations handle the execution. The three form a loop, memory feeds intelligence, intelligence triggers execution, and execution writes new memory back. The long version is in[the Workspace DNA architecture](https://www.taskade.com/blog/workspace-dna-architecture) .


How does Taskade remember my work?


Every project, document, file, and agent conversation becomes context the rest of your workspace can read. A job references the customer it belongs to and an invoice references the deal that closed, so nothing has to be re-pasted into a prompt. The same records render in multiple views: List, Board, Table, and Mind Map in the toolbar, plus Docs, Gantt Chart, Calendar, Actionsheet, and Org Chart under More Views. A trigger pulls an event in, a new lead, a dropped file, or a scheduled time, an agent reads your connected projects, and an action pushes the result back out across[100+ bidirectional integrations](https://www.taskade.com/integrations) . Yes. You can describe an app on mobile and publish it live from the same screen, then keep editing from a laptop later. The workspace is the app and its runtime, so there is nothing to deploy and no build step waiting on a desktop machine. See[build apps from your phone](https://www.taskade.com/blog/build-mobile-apps) and grab the apps from[downloads](https://www.taskade.com/downloads) .

Taskade has a free plan, with paid tiers at $10/month (Pro, the popular choice for 10 users) and $25/month (Business) on annual billing. All three layers run on every plan, including free.
